mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in the prior quarter predicts weakening consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% AND HOUST QoQ decline > -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but median return is not significantly below the baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline, or trigger fires but returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its prior 12-month moving average by more than 4% for two consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by > -4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the trigger does not precede a market downturn in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 4.5% combined with a concurrent rise in the Consumer Price Index above 3% signals a monetary policy response to deflationary pressures, which can boost risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in nonfarm payrolls growth above 0.5 percentage points quarter-over-quarter (using PAYEMS) signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the trigger does not precede a market rally in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 3% month-over-month indicates a sharp contraction in aggregate demand, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered events, or the trigger fires but returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its prior 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals a supply-side recovery, which typically supports corporate margins and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA by > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the trigger does not precede a market rally in at least 55% of cases.
